description: Three committed predictions about two fans in parallel or in series on a steep and a flat system, followed by an interactive Plotly chart of illustrative Curve A, its parallel and series combinations, both system curves, the operating points and a readout table.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Fans in parallel and in series
learningObjectives: The learner will compare one fan, two fans in parallel and two fans in series on a steep and a flat system curve, correctly predicting which combination delivers more airflow on each system.

accessibility.notes: Native buttons with aria-pressed toggles; verdicts, each new prediction, the reveal and every Explore change announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; curves differ by dash pattern and weight as well as colour; operating points also listed in an HTML table with the current cell marked ▸; keys 1-3, Enter, S/F and O/P/R.

simulation.modelType: numeric model (combined fan curves and operating points)
equations: System: P = R x (Q / 10,000)^2 with R = 4.0 (steep) or 1.0 (flat) in. wg
rules: Curve A linearly interpolated; extended along the 14,000-16,000 CFM segment to zero pressure
Operating point: 1 CFM search for the smallest |combined pressure - system pressure|, only where each fan's airflow >= 4,000 CFM
Operating points rounded to 10 CFM and 0.01 in. wg
Three predictions, fixed order, one attempt each; mastery 3 of 3
assumptions: Two identical fans, each on Curve A (illustrative, 1,380 RPM, standard air)
System curves pass through zero (no fixed pressure component)
limitations: Illustrative curve, not a catalog rating
Ignores duct losses between fans, backdraft dampers and unequal sharing between parallel fans

sources: Curve A: illustrative curve from Chapter 10, 'The Fan Curve' section (not a Twin City Fan published rating)
Combining rules and systems: Chapter 25, 'Fans in Parallel and in Series'

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit predictions before the reveal, then compare configurations across two system curves
keyQuestions: On a steep system, which pair moves more air?
On a flat system, which pair moves more air?
Why does a second parallel fan add only about 10% on the steep system?
commonMisconceptions: Two fans in parallel deliver twice the airflow
Series fans are only useful for pressure and never increase airflow
The better combination is a property of the fans rather than of the system
assessmentOpportunities: Score shown as 'Predictions correct: n of 3'; mastery is 3 of 3 on the first attempt.
